subtype: Approach: gather information from a qualified doctor [Action]
passage:
Farhan's slot at the depot ended at one, and the clinic's queue was long, so he waited on the plastic chair with a folded note in his hand. The ache below his ribs had started three weeks ago and got sharper whenever he lifted heavy cartons. His cousin kept forwarding videos with scary claims, but Farhan had stopped watching them.

When his turn came, Dr Shalini asked when it began. He read out the dates from his note and what made it worse. She examined him carefully, then explained which tests would help and what each one could show. Farhan asked how long the results would take, wrote the answer down, and hurried back to the depot with ten minutes to spare.

qa.q: What did Farhan carry into the consultation room?
qa.a: He carried a folded note with the dates and what made the ache worse.

qa.q: What does Farhan stopping the forwarded videos suggest about his feelings?
qa.a: It suggests he was worried and wanted real answers, having decided the frightening claims were not helping him.

qa.q: If the clinic had been closed that day, what other approach could Farhan have tried, and why?
qa.a: He could have phoned to book a slot at a time that fit his shift, since a professional's view still beats guesswork and a booked visit avoids another wasted trip.

qa.q: How might Dr Shalini have seen Farhan's note?
qa.a: The note likely made her job easier, because the dates and triggers gave her clear facts to work from in a short visit.

grounding: A young worker prepares dates and triggers, asks about tests and relies on a doctor rather than online guesswork.

subtype: Approach: gather information from a qualified doctor [Action]
passage:
Jeevan's stomach had been hurting on and off for weeks, mostly after dinner. His flatmate Ojas kept sending him videos: 'Drink this seed water.' 'Stop eating wheat.' 'It's definitely stress.'
On Thursday Jeevan stopped scrolling and booked an appointment with a general physician at a clinic in Jayanagar for Saturday morning.
On Friday night he made a note on his phone. When it started: around the middle of last month. When it's worse: after spicy food, late dinners, and lying down straight after eating. What helps: nothing much. Anything else: waking up at night with it.
At the clinic he read from the note. The doctor asked questions, examined his stomach and said a couple of tests would help. Jeevan asked, 'What are the tests for, and what happens after?' The doctor explained both and wrote them down.
On the way home he muted the video group.

qa.q: When is Jeevan's stomach pain worse?
qa.a: After spicy food, late dinners, and lying down straight after eating.

qa.q: Why did Jeevan mute the video group on the way home?
qa.a: He felt clearer and calmer with a doctor's plan, and tired of confusing guesses from videos.

qa.q: What else could Jeevan bring to the next visit?
qa.a: The test results and an updated note on how the pain has been, plus any new questions.

qa.q: How might Ojas see Jeevan's visit to the doctor?
qa.a: Ojas meant well with the videos, and may be relieved that Jeevan now has proper answers instead of guesses.

grounding: Shows a young worker with a persistent symptom booking a doctor, noting when it started and what worsens it, and asking about tests.

subtype: Approach: gather information from a qualified doctor [Action]
passage:
'Headache again?' Usha asked as Ankita came in and dropped onto the sofa.
'Fourth time this week, Maa. Someone at office said it's screen time. Someone online said it's worse than that.'
'And what does a doctor say?'
'I haven't asked one.'
'Then that's the first thing.' Usha picked up her phone. 'Dr Kulkarni at the clinic downstairs has Saturday slots.'
'Okay. Book it.' Ankita sat up. 'I'll write things down, so I don't forget in there.'
'Like what?'
'When it started, about three weeks ago. That it comes in the afternoon, mostly at my desk. That it's worse on days I skip lunch. That I've been sleeping late.'
'And what will you ask?'
'Whether I need any tests. And what I should watch for.'
On Saturday Ankita read from her list while the doctor listened and asked more questions. She came out with an eye test booked and a plan to keep a headache diary for a while.

qa.q: When do Ankita's headaches mostly come?
qa.a: In the afternoon, mostly at the desk.

qa.q: What might Ankita have been worried about before booking?
qa.a: She was uneasy after hearing online that it could be something worse, and unsure what to believe.

qa.q: What makes Ankita's list useful at the appointment?
qa.a: It gives the doctor clear facts, like when the headaches started and what makes them worse, so nothing is forgotten in the room.

qa.q: How does Usha see the headaches?
qa.a: Usha is concerned but calm, and turns worry into action by booking the doctor straight away.

grounding: Shows a young worker with repeated headaches booking a doctor, noting when they started and what worsens them, and asking about tests.
